Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Google Gemini CLI abused as a hacking agent, malware botnet operator

BleepingComputer
2026-07-15 6 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A Russian-speaking threat actor known as "bandcampro" used Google's open-source Gemini CLI AI tool as a hacking agent and to operate a small-scale botnet. [...]

ATT&CKT1021.001 T1027 T1047 T1053.005 T1059.001 T1190

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] bandcampro Gemini-CLI botnet: PowerShell agent C2 to c2.trialersafe.com · [LLM] PowerShell agent 5-second fixed-interval C2 beacon to public host (bandcampro botnet) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
bandcampro Gemini-CLI botnet: PowerShell agent C2 to c2.trialersafe.com AICommand & Control High
Hunts endpoints resolving or connecting to the botnet's command-and-control host c2.trialersafe.com, the C2 fronted by a Cloudflare tunnel that bandcampro's Gemini-CLI-operated PowerShell agents polled. Article-specific because it pins the exact C2 FQDN and surfaces the initiating process to confirm the lightweight PowerShell agent. Rationale: Pivots on the exact C2 FQDN c2.trialersafe.com pulled from the article's IOC set; projecting InitiatingProcessFileName confirms the PowerShell agent described by Trend Micro. Domain-match on a dedicated 'c2.' subdomain is inherently low-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/07/14/the-bots-are-alive-jailbroken-gemini-spun-up-new-c2-server-for-russian-fraudster-in-just-6-minutes/5270131 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / red-team replaying the published IOC in a sandbox that shares the org's egress
  • Threat-intel feed validation tooling actively resolving the IOC to confirm it is still live
  • DNS sinkhole or protective-DNS appliance logging the blocked lookup (still worth reviewing which host asked)
  • Typo-adjacent legitimate domain sharing the 'trialersafe' token if a marketing/trial service exists
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the source host and the InitiatingProcessFileName/CommandLine — confirm powershell.exe/pwsh.exe or an in-memory script initiated the lookup/connection versus a browser or DNS security tool. Step 2 (contain): Network-isolate the host, block c2.trialersafe.com and its resolved IPs at DNS/proxy/firewall, and kill the offending PowerShell process. Step 3 (hunt): On the isolated host review scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, and Run/RunOnce registry values (the article's three persistence mechanisms), then pivot on the resolved IP and any Cloudflare tunnel endpoints to find sibling bots polling the same C2.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "trialersafe.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has "trialersafe.com"
| project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Src = "DNS"),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationHostName has "trialersafe.com" or RequestURL has "trialersafe.com"
| project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Src = "Proxy/FW")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Botnet C2 Connection to c2.trialersafe.com (bandcampro Gemini-CLI botnet)
id: 2f3a7c4e-9b1d-4e6a-8c0f-5d2b7a1e9c33
description: Detects DNS resolution or connection to the bandcampro botnet C2 host c2.trialersafe.com operated via Gemini CLI.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
  - https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/07/14/the-bots-are-alive-jailbroken-gemini-spun-up-new-c2-server-for-russian-fraudster-in-just-6-minutes/5270131
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/15
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|contains: 'trialersafe.com'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*trialersafe.com* OR *TRIALERSAFE.COM*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/trialersafe\.com/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="c2.trialersafe.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*trialersafe.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.app) as app values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="c2.trialersafe.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*trialersafe.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - count
PowerShell agent 5-second fixed-interval C2 beacon to public host (bandcampro botnet) AICommand & Control Medium
Behavioural detection for the botnet's PowerShell agents that polled the in-memory Python HTTP C2 every five seconds — a tight, regular ~12-connections-per-minute cadence to a public destination. Survives C2 domain/IP rotation because it keys on the beacon regularity from a PowerShell initiator rather than the specific FQDN. Rationale: Keys on the article's explicit '5-second polling' cadence from a PowerShell agent to a public host — a regular ~12/min beacon is distinctive versus human-driven or bursty PowerShell traffic and survives C2 rotation. Sentinel version loses process attribution (no process-attributed network table in this tenant's schema) so it keys on beacon regularity alone. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/07/14/the-bots-are-alive-jailbroken-gemini-spun-up-new-c2-server-for-russian-fraudster-in-just-6-minutes/5270131 • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1059.001 T1029
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PowerShell-based monitoring/health-check scripts that poll a SaaS or internal API on a fixed short interval
  • Configuration-management agents (DSC, custom polling wrappers) invoked through powershell.exe
  • PowerShell modules pulling telemetry to Azure/AWS endpoints at a steady cadence
  • Long-running interactive PowerShell session with an open websocket/keepalive to a cloud service
  • Update/license-check scripts that reconnect every few seconds during a sync window
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("Update-","Get-Metric","HealthCheck","Az.","AWSPowerShell","Invoke-DscResource")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent chain for the beaconing PowerShell — legitimate pollers are usually signed scripts with clear API hostnames, whereas the agent runs in-memory with no script path. Resolve the RemoteIP and check reputation / whether it fronts a Cloudflare tunnel. Step 2 (contain): If unattributed, isolate the host and kill the PowerShell process; block the destination IP/ASN at egress. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep for other hosts beaconing to the same IP at the same cadence (the botnet had ~8 nodes), and inspect scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, and Run keys on affected hosts for the agent's persistence.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(Timestamp, 1m)), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend Rate = todouble(ConnCount) / (DurationMin + 1)   // 5s polling => ~12 conn/min
| where DistinctMinutes >= 10 and ConnCount >= 60          // sustained, not a burst
| where Rate >= 6 and Rate <= 20                           // cadence band consistent with a 5s beacon
| order by ConnCount desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3d)
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| summarize ConnCount = count(), DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SrcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend Rate = todouble(ConnCount) / (DurationMin + 1)   // 5s polling => ~12 conn/min
| where DistinctMinutes >= 10 and ConnCount >= 60
| where Rate >= 6 and Rate <= 20
| order by ConnCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
| count > 60
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(_time) as distinct_secs values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") All_Traffic.dest_category="public" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest _time span=1m | stats sum(count) as ConnCount dc(_time) as DistinctMinutes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by src dest dest_port | eval DurationMin=round((lastTime-firstTime)/60,0), rate=ConnCount/(DurationMin+1) | where DistinctMinutes>=10 AND ConnCount>=60 AND rate>=6 AND rate<=20 | sort - ConnCount
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(_time) as distinct_secs values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") All_Traffic.dest_category="public" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest _time span=1m | stats sum(count) as ConnCount dc(_time) as DistinctMinutes min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by src dest dest_port | eval DurationMin=round((lastTime-firstTime)/60,0), rate=ConnCount/(DurationMin+1) | where DistinctMinutes>=10 AND ConnCount>=60 AND rate>=6 AND rate<=20 | sort - ConnCount
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("payloads.tralalarkefe.com", "c2.trailerkeefe.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["payloads.tralalarkefe.com", "c2.trailerkeefe.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
